name: Color palettes | Narrative Palettes
tagline: Contrasted light / dark color palettes with suggested fonts, each based on a historical or cultural reference.
popTagline: A token set for my projects, and an excuse to dig into the history of pigments.
popOverview: A showcase website built with Nutin around a set of accessible color palettes: pick one and the whole page switches to it, showing its tokens, its fonts and the story behind them. Each theme has a "Copy to clipboard" button to copy the values in JSON.

sectionKeyPoints.Theme picker: Palettes are applied live to the whole page.

sectionKeyPoints.Contrast checks: Run as tests: a palette that fails can't ship.

sectionKeyPoints.Hidden palettes: A few extra palettes, behind a secret route.

sectionKeyPoints.Contrast as a test: A test computes the WCAG ratio of every text token (4.5:1) and every interface token (3:1) against both surfaces, and of text on button fills.

sectionKeyPoints.Palettes as data: Each palette is a typed object (name, period, story, fonts and color values), so the website and the tests read the same source.

sectionKeyPoints.Shared token names: Any palette can replace another without touching the components that use it.

sectionKeyPoints.Historical accuracy vs contrast: Documented pigments rarely meet modern contrast ratios as they are.

sectionKeyPoints.Adjusting values: Colors were adjusted until they passed, while remaining recognizable.

sectionKeyPoints.Testable content: Typing the palettes made their content checkable by the test suite.
